title: Social Distance and Register: Vosotros vs. Ustedes in Spain

sections.content:
In Peninsular Spanish, the distinction between **vosotros** and **ustedes** reflects social relationship and hierarchy:

• **Vosotros** (tuteo plural): Used with anyone you would call *tú* individually:
  - Friends, colleagues, peers, classmates, relatives, neighbours, children.
  - Shopkeepers and waitstaff addressing young or peer customers.
• **Ustedes** (formal plural): Conjugates in third-person plural (*ustedes hablan*, *ustedes tienen*). Reserved strictly for:
  - Elderly strangers as a mark of generational respect.
  - Official legal, judicial, and police interactions.
  - Highly formal institutional ceremonies or luxury corporate settings.
• In Latin America, *ustedes* replaces *vosotros* entirely, but in Spain, using *ustedes* with friends sounds cold or comical!

items.english: —Good afternoon gentlemen, do you have a reservation? (Formal)
—Hey guys! What can I get you? (Informal Peninsular)

items.spanish: En esta oficina todos nos tuteamos y nos llamamos de vosotros.
items.english: In this office we all use informal address with each other.

sections.content: When in Spain, if people your age speak to you in a bar or café, they will almost always address your group as *vosotros*.
